evidence: instruction.md reads as a first-person team lead talking: 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' (L1); 'so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts' (L1); 'dragging is welcome but optional' (L3); 'I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none' (L3); 'layout and names are yours. A clear desktop workspace is what matters. We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.' (L11); 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.' (L13). Contractions are frequent (nobody's, don't, it's, mustn't); sentence length varies from short fragments ('Two things happen in it.', 'Candidates sign in too.') to long compound sentences; it is prose, not bullets. Grep over instruction.md and environment/instructions/*.md for marketing/LLM tells (seamless|robust|delve|leverage|intuitive|elevate|ensure|comprehensive|streamlin|user-friendly|cutting|state-of, em dash, curly apostrophe) returned no matches. The runtime paragraph (L13) is a dense list of facts but stays conversational ('honour PORT if it's set', 'Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages', 'The browser side is free to pull fonts or a script from a CDN if that helps'). Voice continuity with the notes: hireops_rules.md is more formal and structured (headings, two tables, bullets, 'Follow them exactly.' L3), which is appropriate for a referenced rules document and is expressly signposted by the brief ('The exact stage rules, who may do what, and the conversation rules are in /instructions/hireops_rules.md', L11); it keeps the same team voice ('our recruiting workspace', 'what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way this note says' L3-5, 'Each application has one conversation between our side and the candidate' L127, 'Where drafts are kept is yours' L175), British spelling consistent with brief ('honour' in brief; note uses 'Honor' at L200 and integration.md 'honoring' - a minor spelling inconsistency, not a voice defect). Bullets in the rules are not perfectly parallel marketing bullets; they are rule statements of varying length. integration.md lines 1-14 are byte-identical to the template-controlled integration.md (neutral but not robotic), plus one task-added plain paragraph on symlinks (L16-19), consistent in register. Mild observations (not defects): rules §8 'Runtime file paths' (L197-201) reads like operational boilerplate in a slightly different register from the rest of the note; a few reflow-inconsistent long lines (L99, L112, L173) show editing but do not affect voice. Counterexample search: a reader would not plausibly identify this brief as LLM-polished prose (no hedging stacks, no 'Key features:' lists, no gloss words); a version that would fail would be e.g. 'HireOps is a robust, seamless recruiting platform that empowers teams...' with parallel feature bullets, which is absent. This row is a text-quality check; no runtime evidence is needed or claimed, so no missing measurement applies.
